title: test(runtime): route-ledger.conformance has no per-route reverse check, so 26 deleted ledger rows stay green; the decision it defers to (#17041) does not resolve
body:
Filing gate ①: a test gap with a named location, measured. Found by the #26441 card thread (devx seat 2, PR #26511, report 6435002819) while deciding whether `check-route-ledger-census` could retire. Filed by `domain:devx` seat 2 (#20163, session `session_01Q4MDXRbEJCNdPAP4SiXwp9`). ⛔ Not a claim. Dedupe: the 300 newest open and closed issues grepped for `route-ledger.conformance|reverse check|17041` returned no other card.

## Measured (the #26441 thread, on `main` after `c91544a4`)

- Delete 3 mid-ledger rows from `packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts` `ROUTE_LEDGER` (`GET /meta/types`, `POST /actions/global/:action`, `POST /actions/_activation/:object/:action`). `route-ledger.conformance.test.ts` stays 6/6 green, `client-url-conformance` 3/3, dogfood live-mount parity 8/8. Only `check-route-ledger-census` (the hand-kept "N rows" count) reds.
- Delete 26 non-final rows: the runtime conformance is still green; only the client conformance reds. Delete 28 non-sdk rows: only dogfood reds. Delete a whole section: the runtime conformance reds.

So the runtime ledger's only per-row deletion guard is a typed row count. That is the transcription-pin shape #26431 retires, and it is kept by #26511 for this reason alone.

## Why it is this way

`route-ledger.ts` (header above `ROUTE_LEDGER`) and `scripts/check-route-ledger-census.mjs` (§ "Why a census and NOT a comparison against registered routes") both say that a per-route check against the dispatcher is "an open maintainer decision in #17041", because `DomainHandlerRegistry.list()` exposes domains, not routes. **#17041 returns 404 on this repository**, so that pointer no longer resolves.

## Wanted

Either of these. The second is a decision for the owning lane or the maintainer.
- **(a) A reverse check:** the runtime conformance test asserts that every route the dispatcher mounts (enumerated at route granularity, e.g. by a registry listing or a probe of the running server, as the REST ledger's conformance already does) has a ledger row. The census count can then retire (#26431).
- **(b) A recorded ruling** that the count stays the guard. Re-point the two `#17041` references to wherever that decision now lives.

**Size:** S–M. **Clause-②:** no. **Metadata-protocol:** none.

## Related

#26441 / PR #26511 (keeps the census on this measurement); #26431 (retire transcription pins); #16758 (the census's origin); #26410 / PR #26491 (the same class, retired for the authz census).
